original_value: In this paper, we question the premise that graphics hardware uses a post-transform cache to avoid redundant vertex shader invocations. A large body of existing work on optimizing indexed triangle sets for rendering speed is based upon this widely-accepted assumption. We conclusively show that this assumption does not hold up on modern graphics hardware. We design and conduct experiments that demonstrate the behavior of current hardware of all major vendors to be inconsistent with the presence of a common post-transform cache. Our results strongly suggest that modern hardware rather relies on a batch-based approach, most likely for reasons of scalability. A more thorough investigation based on these initial experiments allows us to partially uncover the actual strategies implemented on graphics processors today. We reevaluate existing mesh optimization algorithms in light of these new findings and present a new mesh optimization algorithm designed from the ground up to target architectures that rely on batch-based vertex reuse. In an extensive evaluation, we measure and compare the real-world performance of various optimization algorithms on modern hardware. Our results show that some established algorithms still perform well. However, if the batching strategy of the target architecture is known, our approach can significantly outperform these previous state-of-the-art methods.

result.paraphrase: This paper challenges the assumption that graphics hardware uses a post-transform cache to prevent redundant vertex shader calls. Much prior work on speeding up indexed triangle sets relies on this widely accepted premise, but we show conclusively that it no longer holds on modern graphics hardware. Through designed experiments, we demonstrate that current hardware from all major vendors behaves inconsistently with the existence of a shared post-transform cache. The results strongly indicate that modern hardware instead uses a batch-based approach, likely for scalability reasons. Further investigation based on these initial experiments helps partially reveal the strategies used by today’s graphics processors. In light of these findings, we reconsider existing mesh optimization algorithms and introduce a new one built from the ground up for architectures that rely on batch-based vertex reuse. In an extensive evaluation, we measure and compare the real-world performance of several optimization algorithms on modern hardware. The results show that some established methods still perform well, but when the target architecture’s batching strategy is known, our approach can significantly outperform earlier state-of-the-art methods.
